clue.text: Reportedly a few are located here in the West Country

indicators.note: reportedly means as said aloud, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: a few is some and located is set, giving the spoken phrase some are set

explanation.surface: A remark that only a handful of somethings can be found in south-west England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reportedly' tells you to say 'some are set' aloud. SOMERSET is a county in the West Country of south-west England; 'here' points the definition at a place.
explanation.definitionFit: The county lies in south-west England, the region called the West Country, so it is an example of a place there.

clue.text: Split in southern church is over mass

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the earlier pieces sit above the next

parts.note: taken as written
M is the physics symbol for mass

explanation.surface: A southern congregation divides after its service of Mass ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' suggests finished, but in a down clue it stacks the pieces; 'mass' looks like the service.
explanation.definitionFit: A schism is a split or division, especially within a church.

clue.text: Like antiquated material attacked by geometers?

definitions.meaning: old fabric worn out and full of holes
geometers are a family of moths whose larvae eat cloth, not mathematicians

explanation.surface: Old cloth assaulted by mathematicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Moth-eaten means shabby and outdated, and literally damaged by moth larvae.

clue.text: Again tried making soldiers drive together around area

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers

indicators.note: around means the herding word encloses the area letter

parts.note: to herd is to drive animals together

explanation.surface: Troops round up a herd near a field, starting over again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tried' is in the legal sense: a case heard again.
explanation.definitionFit: A case that was reheard was tried again in court.

clue.text: English academic carrying old Jewish vestment

indicators.note: carrying means the academic holds the old letter inside

parts.note: a PhD is a doctor, an academic

explanation.surface: A British scholar carries an ancient Hebrew priestly garment.
explanation.definitionFit: An ephod is a sleeveless garment worn by ancient Jewish priests.

clue.text: May one keep of dingoes originally in high-quality runs?

indicators.note: in puts the picked letter inside the word for top quality

parts.note: something high-quality is fine

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word dingoes

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether a keeper of wild dogs runs them first-rate.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the saying 'finders keepers': the one who finds something may keep it.
explanation.definitionFit: By the playground rule 'finders keepers', the discoverer of a lost thing is allowed to hold on to it.

clue.text: One with privileged info where to find apple juice, say?

indicators.note: say means the phrase is spoken aloud

parts.note: fermented apple juice is cider, so it is found in cider

explanation.surface: A question about who has the inside story on apple juice's location.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' shows that 'in cider' sounds like INSIDER.
explanation.definitionFit: An insider is someone within an organisation with access to confidential information.

clue.text: Single bloke takes hours looking up washerwoman

indicators.note: in a down clue looking up means the whole piece reads from bottom to top

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, single

indicators.note: takes means the bloke holds the hours letter inside

parts.note: bod is British slang for a person, a bloke

explanation.surface: A lone man spends hours seeking out a laundress.
explanation.walkthrough: I + BOHD reversed by 'looking up' gives DHOBI, an Indian word for a person who washes clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: In India a dhobi is a laundry worker, washing clothes for a living.

clue.text: Gave up office, being quietly submissive

explanation.surface: Someone left their post, meekly accepting their fate.
explanation.definitionFit: Resigned means stepped down from a post, and also accepting the inevitable without complaint.

clue.text: Given work in plant, daughter suffered torment

indicators.note: in places the working word inside the plant

parts.note: anise is a plant
to work is to go, as in a machine that goes

explanation.surface: A daughter put to work in a factory endured anguish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like a factory; it is the herb ANISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To have agonised is to have suffered great mental anguish.

clue.text: Go to extremes — smash theatre lights round Oxford Street

parts.note: a smash success is a hit
the main street of Oxford, High Street, is known locally as the High
spotlights in a theatre are spots

explanation.surface: Someone wrecks the stage lighting while touring a famous London shopping street.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford Street wants to be London's shopping street; here it is the main street in the city of Oxford, always called 'the High'. 'round' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to indulge in the most exciting or extreme pleasures, going to excess in enjoyment.

clue.text: One is often at sea, serving on board

definitions.meaning: a crew member who works aboard ships
waiting on passengers aboard a ship or aircraft

explanation.surface: A muddled person working on a ship or committee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' suggests bewilderment and 'on board' a committee; both are literal here, describing a crew member serving passengers.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's attendant who looks after passengers' food and cabins works at sea, serving aboard the vessel.

clue.text: Like casual acquaintances making careless mistakes

definitions.meaning: people who barely know each other have a ... acquaintance, greeting with a nod
as in 'even Homer nods', dozing off means slipping up through inattention

explanation.surface: Barely-known friends who keep getting things wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A nodding acquaintance is a slight one, and to nod is to make a lapse through drowsiness.

clue.text: Show-off's exploits may secure low grades for pupils

indicators.note: may secure means the stunts hold the grades inside them

parts.note: a show-off performs stunts
D and E are low marks in exam grading

explanation.surface: Daredevil antics could earn poor marks for schoolchildren.
explanation.definitionFit: Students and pupils are synonyms for people being taught at school or college.

clue.text: Old headgear needs patching badly

indicators.note: badly signals the letters of patching are rearranged

explanation.surface: An ancient hat in need of repair.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightcap was a cloth cap formerly worn in bed.

clue.text: City church follows up resistance to survey

parts.note: R is the physics symbol for resistance
EC is the postcode of the City of London
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A city's church is said to follow up on opposition so as to look it over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'follows up' places the City and church after R. RECCE is informal British for a reconnaissance, here as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To recce is informal military slang for making a reconnaissance, that is, inspecting an area.

clue.text: Warden acting on departing person's friendly advice?

definitions.meaning: a custodian or keeper of a building

definitions.text: acting on departing person's friendly advice?
definitions.meaning: the parting words 'take care', obeyed literally

explanation.surface: A keeper who heeded a goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: A caretaker looks after a building, a warden, and cryptically is one who takes care.

clue.text: Horse-drawn carriage -one with sweeping design, some say

indicators.note: some say means the word is spoken aloud

parts.note: a broom is made for sweeping

explanation.surface: An elegant carriage with flowing lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweeping design' suggests graceful styling; it is a brush. BROUGHAM is pronounced like 'broom'.
explanation.definitionFit: A brougham is a light four-wheeled horse-drawn closed carriage.

clue.text: Bachelor withdraws from shoot in stock farm

indicators.note: withdraws from means the bachelor letter leaves the word for shoot

parts.note: a shoot of a tree is a branch
B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in BA

explanation.surface: A single man pulls out of a hunting party on a livestock holding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shoot' looks like a hunt, which suits a farm, but it is a twig.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranch is a large farm for raising cattle or other livestock.

clue.text: Beginning to go, off method for building public road

parts.note: meat starting to go off is high
a method is a way

explanation.surface: A road built using a method that is starting to fail.
explanation.walkthrough: HIGH describes game or meat that has started to spoil.
explanation.definitionFit: A highway is a main public road.

clue.text: Having change of heart, assess attempt to make gismos

indicators.note: change of heart means the central letter of the word is swapped for another

parts.note: to assess is to gauge
an attempt is a try

explanation.surface: Someone reconsiders and tries to evaluate a set of gadgets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having change of heart' swaps the middle U of GAUGE for D, giving GADGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Gismos are gadgets, and gadgetry is such devices collectively.

clue.text: Properties in Maryland and Virginia, for example

definitions.text: Properties in Maryland and Virginia, for example

parts.words: Properties in Maryland and Virginia, for example
parts.note: the clue names two US states, and the plantations held there are landed holdings

explanation.surface: Real estate in two American states.
explanation.walkthrough: Maryland and Virginia are STATES, and the answer is that word with E added, describing the big plantation holdings there.
explanation.definitionFit: Estates are large landed properties, like the plantations of the American South.

clue.text: For occupying children it has its ups and downs

definitions.text: For occupying children it has its ups and downs

parts.words: For occupying children it has its ups and downs
parts.note: sounds like parenting's mixed fortunes, but describes playground equipment rising and falling

explanation.surface: Keeping kids busy is a rollercoaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A seesaw is a plank pivoted in the middle on which children rise and fall.

clue.text: Honest expression of support for Tories?

definitions.meaning: an honest person is straight and principled
a cheer of 'up the right!' backs the conservative wing

explanation.surface: A sincere cheer for the Conservatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Upright means honourable and honest, and read as two words it is a rallying cry for the political right.

clue.text: Hungrily devour a flesh-eating bird

definitions.meaning: a large black crow that eats carrion

explanation.surface: Gobbling up a carnivorous bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Raven as a verb means to eat voraciously, and as a noun is a large carrion-eating crow.

clue.text: Some spent 'it legitimately to qualify

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Cockney insists some of the money was spent lawfully.
explanation.definitionFit: To entitle someone is to give them the right, that is to qualify them, for something.

clue.text: Wine imbibed by the Spanish and English aristocracy

indicators.note: imbibed by means the wine is drunk inside the other pieces

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
It is Italian vermouth, as in gin and it

explanation.surface: Wine drunk by Spanish and English nobility.
explanation.walkthrough: IT for Italian vermouth comes from the British drink 'gin and it'.
explanation.definitionFit: The elite is the best or most privileged group, like an aristocracy.

clue.text: Possess necessary ability and keep two to tango?

definitions.meaning: the saying 'it takes two to tango' means the needed thing is two, so holding that is keeping two

explanation.surface: Being capable means always holding a dance partner.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means having the qualities required to succeed, and cryptically retaining what 'it takes' in the saying.

clue.text: Primates surrender king for certain sums

indicators.note: surrender means the monkeys give up the king letter

parts.note: monkeys are primates
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Apes give up their monarch in exchange for sums of cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Moneys, an old plural of money, means particular amounts or funds.

clue.text: Firm prison officer's means of exerting pressure

parts.note: firm, as in set hard, means set
screw is British slang for a prison warder

explanation.surface: A tough jailer's way of applying pressure on inmates.
explanation.walkthrough: SCREW is British slang for a prison officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A setscrew is a screw that clamps parts together by pressing against them.
